# Phase worker

The coordinator keeps its own context small: it holds the plan table, calls Codex in the background, runs the gates and commits. Claude's heavy work for a phase runs in a fresh general-purpose subagent, one per task, so each starts with an empty context. Invoking autopilot is the user's explicit request for these subagents, so use the host's subagent tool for every `implement`, `verify` and `revise` task, and for every `code-reviewer` run ([phase review](phase-review.md)), even where the host otherwise discourages spawning agents.

If no subagent tool is available, do not do the task in the main session on your own decision. Tell the user that a clean context per phase cannot be guaranteed, ask whether to continue in the main session, and wait for the answer. If the user agrees, record `Workers: main session` in `plan.md`, so a resumed session does not ask again; the line applies only while no subagent tool is available. If the user declines, stop and record nothing.

## Tasks

| Task | When | The worker does |
|---|---|---|
| `implement` | Executor is `claude`, or Codex fell back | Implement the phase with `kit-implement --from-plan`, this phase only |
| `verify` | After implementation, after each fix, and for a fix round from a review | Fix the `Review findings` first when there are any (one round), then run `kit-test` for the phase; on failure, if [fix routing](fix-routing.md) picks Claude and budget remains, fix with `kit-fix` and test again |
| `revise` | After a Gate 2 rejection that [fix routing](fix-routing.md#user-rejection) gives to Claude, and once at the [final review](phase-review.md#final-review) | Apply the user's feedback or the final review findings with `kit-fix` (one round), then test and fix within the remaining budget |

The worker never calls Codex. When routing picks Codex, it stops and returns `needs-codex` with trimmed evidence. The coordinator then runs `codex exec resume` in the background and starts a new `verify` worker.

## Prompt

Fill in the fields of the template and nothing else: no extra notes, lessons or context from the conversation. `Previous evidence` and `User feedback` come from the current phase only. What a later phase needs to know belongs in its phase file. The same rule applies to [Codex prompts](codex-handoff.md#implement-prompt).

```text
You are a phase worker for an autopilot run. Task: <implement | verify | revise>.

Plan overview: <path to plan.md>
Phase file: <path to phase-NN-*.md>
Project root: <path>
Codex: <available | unavailable>
Fix rounds already used: <n> of 3
Previous evidence (verify after a fix): <trimmed failing output, or "none">
User feedback (revise only): <verbatim, or "none">
Review findings: <critical and high findings from the reviewer, verbatim, or "none">

Rules:
- Read the plan overview and this phase file only.
- The working tree may already hold uncommitted work for this phase. Check git status and build on it; do not revert it.
- Before each step, load its skill with the Skill tool and follow it: kit-implement to implement, kit-test to run the checks, kit-fix to fix a failure or apply user feedback.
- Keep the plan's Global Constraints exactly, and produce and consume what the phase's Interfaces section says.
- When the phase file says `TDD: yes`, load kit-tdd before implementing. Without it, still write each test first and watch it fail before writing the code, and say in notes that kit-tdd was not available. Either way, report each test's failing line before the code and passing line after it in `evidence`.
- Do not edit plan files, tick todos, change statuses, commit, push or switch branches.
- Do not call Codex.
- Count every fix you apply as one round. Applying the user feedback of a revise task is one round too. Stop when the total reaches 3.
- If a fix needs a large rework, many modules, or a requirement the implementation misread, stop and return needs-codex. When Codex is unavailable, fix it yourself within the budget instead.
- Never skip, disable or weaken tests, and never report a skipped check as passing.
- Review findings are claims to verify, not orders. Check each against the code first. Fix a real one; leave a wrong one unchanged and record a ruling saying why. Fixing the review findings counts as one round.
- When a fix round has a test that covers the defect, report that test's failing line before the fix and its passing line after it in `evidence`.
- Red flags. When you catch yourself thinking one of these, do the right-hand side instead:
  - "It should pass" or "it probably works" → run the command and read its output and exit code.
  - "This failure was already there" → only a failure recorded in `Baseline` was; any other failure belongs to this phase.
  - "This test is unrelated" → report it as failed anyway.
  - "I'll change the test to match the code" → only when the test contradicts the phase file, and record a ruling.
  - "I'll add X while I'm here" → it is outside the phase; leave it.
  - "The previous step reported it passed" → run this task's checks yourself.
- A failure the plan overview records as `Baseline: ...; blocks: no` was there before this phase. Do not fix it or count it as a round, and it does not make the status failed. Report that check as failed (baseline), and add a line to notes if its failure differs from the recorded one.

Return only this report:
status: passed | failed | needs-codex | blocked
fix_rounds_used: <total including earlier rounds>
changed_files: <paths>
checks: <command: passed | failed | failed (baseline) | not-run>, one per line
evidence: <failing output trimmed to the relevant lines, or "none">
rulings: <one line per decision the phase file did not dictate: what you decided — why — what it costs if wrong; or "none">
notes: <remaining risks for the user's review, under 10 lines>
```

## Using the report

- `passed` from `implement`: run the scope check, then start a `verify` worker.
- `passed` from `verify` or `revise`: start the [review](phase-review.md#review), or the re-review after a fix round from a review. Build the Gate 2 report from `changed_files`, `checks`, `rulings` and `notes` and the reviewer's report, without running the checks again yourself. Do not commit before the user accepts.
- `failed` with budget left: start a new `verify` worker with the evidence. With the budget used up, set the phase to `blocked` and stop.
- `needs-codex`: run `codex exec resume` with the evidence, count it as a fix round, then start a new `verify` worker.
- `blocked`: stop and report.

Record `fix_rounds_used` in `plan.md` after every report.
